title: Workstream E: Majority-Class Selection Bias Mechanism Diagnosis

four_evidence_pillars_separation.1_diagnostic_evidence: Class retention ratios R_c(kappa) and recall disparities document that Policy A hoards majority classes at low coverage tiers.
four_evidence_pillars_separation.2_statistical_evidence: Holm-Bonferroni hypothesis tests verify that unweighted Policy A achieves statistically significant gains on only 4 of 11 instruments.
four_evidence_pillars_separation.3_policy_selection_evidence: Directional ranking policies (Policy B and D) mitigate majority-class hoarding on retrospective evaluation data.
four_evidence_pillars_separation.4_economic_performance_evidence: NONE. No executable trading strategy, alpha generation, or transaction profitability is asserted in Phase 5.4.

BTCUSDT.mechanism_description: Under Policy A (Global Max Probability), class retention disparity reached 6.27x at 20% coverage. In instruments where expiration or a dominant class has higher baseline probability, Policy A preferentially retains that majority class while discarding minority directional classes, causing directional recall and Balanced Accuracy to collapse.

diagnostic_alternative_mitigation.policy_b_directional_confidence: Filters directly on max(P_SL, P_TP), isolating directional conviction from expiration probability mass.
diagnostic_alternative_mitigation.policy_d_directional_mass: Filters on (P_SL + P_TP) = 1 - P_EXP, explicitly penalizing expiration uncertainty.
diagnostic_alternative_mitigation.research_candidate_status: RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_ONLY (No production deployment or live trading authorized).
